overview: Figma is a collaborative design and product development platform that helps teams go from idea to shipped product entirely in the browser. The company's platform spans UI/UX design (Figma Design), whiteboarding (FigJam), developer handoff (Dev Mode), presentations (Figma Slides), AI-native prototyping (Figma Make), website publishing (Figma Sites), marketing asset creation (Figma Buzz), and vector illustration (Figma Draw). Figma serves 95% of Fortune 500 companies and operates globally with the majority of revenue and monthly active users outside the United States.

business_model.summary: Subscription-based per-seat pricing across multiple tiers (Starter/free, Professional, Organization, Enterprise) with a strong product-led growth motion supplemented by direct enterprise sales. Revenue is recognized ratably over the contract term. AI features are monetized via an AI credit consumption layer introduced in March 2026, layered on top of the seat-based model.

revenue_streams.name: Subscription Revenue (Seats)
revenue_streams.description: Per-seat annual and monthly subscriptions across Viewer, Collab, Content, Dev, and Full seat types. Single revenue line in filings.

revenue_streams.name: AI Credits (nascent)
revenue_streams.description: Consumption-based overlay monetizing Figma Make and Figma AI usage. Launched March 18, 2026; early traction exceeding internal targets.

business_model.customer_type: B2B with strong bottom-up adoption. Designers, developers, product managers, and marketers at companies ranging from startups to Fortune 500 enterprises.
business_model.geographic_mix: US approximately 47%, International approximately 53% (international revenue grew 45% YoY in FY2025). 85% of MAUs are outside the US, indicating significant international monetization runway. India is the second-largest market by MAUs; new Bengaluru office opened in 2026.

main_competitors: AI-native design/coding tools (Cursor, v0 by Vercel, Bolt)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader in professional collaborative UI/UX design with ~80-90% share in that segment and ~38% share in the broader collaborative design and prototyping category. Canva leads in social/marketing content creation with 265M MAUs vs Figma's roughly 13M+ professional MAUs.

moat_factors.description: Multiplayer-first architecture means every stakeholder — designers, PMs, engineers, executives — converges on the same file. Adoption by one team member pulls in others organically.
Organizations build design systems, token libraries, and component inventories inside Figma that are deeply embedded in CI/CD and development workflows. Switching costs grow as design ops mature.
250,000+ community resources, 10,000+ plugins/widgets, active MCP server ecosystem, 200+ Friends of Figma chapters globally. Community assets compound over time.

Launched 7 new products in 4 years (2021-2025). Config 2026 (June 24-25) unveiled Code Layers, Figma Motion, AI-generated shaders, generative plugins, and expanded Figma agent capabilities, reinforcing Figma as the single canvas from design to code.

moat_factors.factor: Brand in design and product development
moat_factors.description: Figma is the industry standard for product design teams. The annual Config conference drives community loyalty and product awareness. 76% of paid customers use 2+ products.

weaknesses: Reliance on third-party AI models (OpenAI, etc.) for inference; no proprietary foundation models creates dependency and margin risk
Gross margin structurally compressed to ~82% (from ~90% pre-AI) as AI inference costs scale
Cannot match Adobe's $3.8B cumulative AI investment or Microsoft's infrastructure scale
International revenue lags MAU share, suggesting lower monetization of non-US users
SBC dilution remains a structural concern: $1.364B recognized in FY2025 (129% of revenue) due to IPO-triggered dual-trigger RSUs
One customer exceeded 10% of revenue in recent periods, creating concentration risk

growth_drivers: AI credit monetization: launched March 18, 2026 — more than 75% of users who exceeded credit limits continued paying in April; over 95% remained active. AI becoming a meaningful revenue layer.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) adoption: weekly active users grew 5x QoQ in Q1 2026; customers using MCP expanded Full seats ~70% faster than non-users, directly linking AI to seat growth.
Figma Make deepening: 60% of $100K+ ARR customers used Figma Make weekly in Q1 2026 (up from 30% at IPO and 50% in Q4 2025). Pro-to-paid conversion up 150%+ YoY.
Enterprise market penetration: 1,525 customers with $100K+ ARR as of Q1 2026 (48% YoY growth); 67 customers with $1M+ ARR (68% YoY growth in FY2025).
Net Dollar Retention expansion: NDR rose to 139% in Q1 2026 (highest in 2+ years), indicating strong seat expansion and AI upsell within existing accounts.
Code Layers (announced Config 2026, rolling out July 2026): allows GitHub repositories directly on the design canvas, bridging design and engineering workflows and pulling in developer seat upgrades.
Figma Motion (announced Config 2026): native animation timeline enables production-ready animations, competing with dedicated animation tools and deepening Full seat value.
International monetization uplift: India office, local data hosting for enterprise. 47-53% international revenue vs 85% of MAUs outside the US leaves a large monetization gap to close.
Secular tailwinds: 1B+ new apps forecast by 2028 (IDC), design-to-code convergence, AI-era need to visualize products before building them.

business.description: AI tools (Cursor, v0, GitHub Copilot) allow developers to build UIs directly from prompts, potentially reducing or eliminating the design phase. If 'code is a commodity,' Figma's response is to make design the competitive differentiator — but this is not yet proven at scale.
One customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in recent 10-Q periods. Loss or downsizing of that account would materially impact results.

GAAP gross margin declined from ~90% pre-AI to ~79% in Q1 2026 (82% non-GAAP) due to AI inference and infrastructure costs. Management has not guided to a recovery timetable, and costs will scale with AI adoption.

business.risk: Billing model changes inhibiting viral growth
business.description: March 2025 billing update added admin controls over seat upgrades, reducing organic bottom-up expansion. Trade-off between revenue predictability and the product-led growth engine that historically drove growth.

Canva crossed $4B ARR (vs Figma's $1.4B guidance for FY2026) and is adding professional design features. Its 265M MAUs represent significant competitive reach, especially in teams that use both platforms.

financial.description: $1.364B SBC recognized in FY2025 (129% of revenue) driven by IPO-triggered dual-trigger RSUs. Ongoing SBC from post-IPO grants (29M+ new shares to leadership) creates sustained dilution pressure. GAAP profitability is likely years away.

An extended lockup agreement covering approximately 54.1% of outstanding shares expires August 31, 2026. Supply overhang from insider and early investor selling could pressure the stock materially. Stock is already down ~87% from its $142 IPO-day high.
53% of revenue from international markets creates FX headwinds in strong-dollar environments.

financial.risk: Non-GAAP vs GAAP gap obscures true economics
financial.description: Non-GAAP operating income of $129.5M in FY2025 vs GAAP net loss of $(1.25)B. Investors relying on non-GAAP metrics should be aware SBC is a real economic cost.

regulatory.description: Substantive requirements enforceable from August 2026. AI features (Figma Make, AI agent) may trigger transparency, risk assessment, and human oversight obligations. Fines up to 7% of global revenue for high-risk system violations.
GDPR, India's DPDP Act, and other data localization requirements add compliance costs. Figma is building local data hosting to address enterprise demand, especially in India.

regulatory.risk: IP infringement from generative AI output
regulatory.description: Figma Make and generative plugins could produce content infringing third-party IP. Third-party model indemnification coverage may be insufficient; Figma holds ultimate liability exposure to customers.

macro.description: Enterprise software budgets are subject to macroeconomic cycles. Sales cycle lengthening was observed in 2025; another downturn could slow seat expansion and enterprise deals.
Figma must attract and retain top AI engineers in a market where OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Meta offer substantially higher compensation and more AI infrastructure scale.

execution.risk: CEO Dylan Field voting control and attention
execution.description: Field controls approximately 75% of voting power through the dual-class structure (Class B shares carry 15 votes). Figma qualifies as a 'controlled company.' Field has external investment activities that could divert attention. Loss of Field would be highly disruptive given his centrality to product vision and culture.

Seven products launched in four years (2021-2025), plus Code Layers and Figma Motion in 2026. Each must achieve cross-sell penetration within the existing base. 76% of customers use 2+ products, but monetizing the long tail of products adds GTM complexity.

Credit limits were enforced March 18, 2026 with strong early retention. However, if credit pricing is set too high or AI value is not perceived, churn and customer backlash are possible. Early data is only weeks old.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global design tools / application software market continues to grow, driven by digital product proliferation. IDC forecasts 1B+ new apps by 2028. AI is simultaneously the biggest threat and the biggest opportunity: 72% of designers now use generative AI in their workflows, and Figma's bet is that AI makes design more — not less — important. Visual cloud market projected to grow 13.5% annually to $237.3B by 2029.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — B2B SaaS subscription model provides stability, but enterprise seat count is sensitive to headcount reductions and IT budget cycles. Startup customer cohort (seeded Figma's early growth) is more vulnerable to funding downturns.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct impact. Indirectly, VC-backed startup health affects the bottom of Figma's customer funnel. Higher rates slow startup formation and headcount growth, compressing the addressable seat pool.
key_input_costs: Third-party AI model inference costs (OpenAI, etc.) — key driver of gross margin compression
Cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) — scales with usage
SBC to attract and retain AI/ML talent
Content delivery and hosting for global MAUs

recent_developments.event: Config 2026 (June 23-25, San Francisco): Figma announced Code Layers (GitHub repos on design canvas, rolling out July 2026), Figma Motion (native animation timeline with CSS/React export), AI-generated shader fills, generative plugins, expanded Figma agent with 'Skills' and 'Connectors' (Notion, Slack, GitHub, Atlassian). First Config India announced.

FIG stock fell ~37% in two weeks from early June highs (~$27) to ~$17 as of June 25, 2026. Year-to-date decline of approximately 40%, and roughly 87% below its $142 all-time high from IPO day. Wells Fargo cut price target to $36 from $42 on June 26.

Q1 2026 earnings: revenue $333.4M (+46% YoY, reaccelerating from +40% in Q4 2025), NDR jumped to 139% (highest in 2+ years), 690K paid customers (+54% YoY). Non-GAAP gross margin 82%, non-GAAP operating income $56.5M. FY2026 guidance raised $55M to $1.422-1.428B.

AI credit monetization launched March 18, 2026. By end of April, more than 75% of users who had exceeded credit limits continued purchasing credits. More than 95% remained active on the platform, validating willingness to pay for AI features.

FY2025 annual results reported: $1.056B revenue (+41% YoY), GAAP net loss $(1.25)B (including $975.7M one-time IPO RSU SBC), non-GAAP net income $166.8M, FCF $250.7M, NDR 136%, 1,405 customers with $100K+ ARR. Initial FY2026 guidance of $1.366-1.374B and non-GAAP OI of $100-110M.

Standard 180-day IPO lockup expired January 27, 2026. An extended lockup agreement was separately arranged covering ~54.1% of outstanding shares, running until August 31, 2026, providing temporary overhang relief.
Q3 2025 earnings: $274M revenue (+38% YoY), NDR 131%, 140 net new $100K+ ARR customers, raised FY guidance to $1.044-1.046B. IPO-related SBC of $975.7M recognized in the quarter.
IPO on July 31, 2025 at $33/share on NYSE. Stock surged ~250% on first trading day to $142-143 range, then declined steadily. CEO Dylan Field filed a 10b5-1 trading plan four days post-IPO.

Launched four new products in 2025: Figma Sites, Figma Make (AI prototyping), Figma Buzz (marketing assets), and Figma Draw (vector illustration). Adobe acquisition termination fee of $1B (received in 2023) remains on balance sheet as part of Figma's $1.6-1.7B cash position.

items.notes: Implies approximately 35% YoY growth. Acceleration driven by AI credit monetization and seat expansion.
Implies approximately 40% YoY growth at midpoint, sustaining Q1 2026 acceleration.

items.vs_prior: declined from ~90% pre-AI scale-up; management has guided margin pressure to continue
items.notes: AI inference costs (third-party models) are primary driver of compression from historical ~88-90% levels.

items.vs_prior: up 3 points QoQ, highest in 2+ years; up from 136% in Q4 2025
items.notes: Driven by AI feature upsell and seat expansion. Management expects continued strength from AI credit monetization.

items.vs_prior: up from 1,405 at Q4 2025; 48% YoY growth
items.notes: Key enterprise growth metric. Code Layers and MCP adoption expected to drive further Full seat upgrades.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Dylan Field (Q1 2026 call): 'Design is the competitive edge when code is a commodity.' Emphasized that AI makes design more strategically important, not less. Highlighted that 60% of largest customers used Figma Make weekly and that MCP server users expanded Full seats 70% faster than non-users. CFO Praveer Melwani noted AI credit monetization launched March 18 and 'blew past internal targets,' giving management 'tremendous confidence in the road ahead.' Raised full-year guidance $55M on the back of AI credit traction.

bull_case: Revenue reaccelerating: Q1 2026 grew 46% YoY (vs 40% in Q4 2025 and 38% in Q3 2025), driven by AI credit monetization, not just seat expansion — demonstrating a new and durable revenue layer.
AI monetization is working: AI credit enforcement launched March 18, 2026; 75%+ of users who hit credit limits kept paying, 95%+ remained active. This is strong revealed preference for AI value.
NDR expanding to 139%, the highest in two years, indicating the installed base is spending more per seat, validating the multi-product and AI upsell thesis.

Config 2026 (June 2026) positions Figma as the convergence point for design and engineering: Code Layers (GitHub on canvas), Figma Motion, and the expanded agent challenge Cursor and dedicated animation tools, potentially expanding TAM significantly.

Stock down ~87% from IPO-day high and ~40% YTD in 2026; at ~$18-19, the valuation de-risks considerably relative to $1.4B+ revenue with 35% growth and improving non-GAAP margins. Analyst consensus is Buy with an average price target of ~$36-38.
Strong balance sheet: $1.6-1.7B in cash (including retained $1B Adobe termination fee) provides runway for AI investment without dilutive financing.
Secular tailwinds: design-to-code convergence, IDC's 1B+ app forecast by 2028, shift to AI-assisted product development workflows all expand Figma's addressable market.
bear_case: Existential AI threat from code-generation tools: Cursor, v0, GitHub Copilot, and similar tools let developers build UI directly from text prompts, potentially eliminating the design phase. Figma's answer (Code Layers) is unproven at scale.

Stock remains 87% below its $142 all-time high with no clear near-term catalyst for recovery; ongoing insider selling and the August 31, 2026 lockup expiry (covering ~54% of shares) could create sustained selling pressure.
SBC dilution is structurally severe: $1.364B in FY2025 (129% of revenue). Non-GAAP adjustments that exclude this make earnings appear better than economic reality. GAAP profitability is years away.

Gross margin structurally compressed to ~79% GAAP (82% non-GAAP) and management has not guided to recovery — AI cost scaling could erode the SaaS-grade margins that historically justified Figma's premium valuation.

Governance risk: Dylan Field controls ~75% of votes (Class B = 15 votes/share), leaving minority shareholders with little recourse. Figma is a 'controlled company' under NYSE rules, exempting it from certain independence requirements.

Canva at $4B ARR (nearly 3x Figma's scale) and Adobe's $3.8B AI investment represent formidable competition. Canva's 265M MAUs provide a funnel to move upmarket into professional design, and Adobe can bundle Firefly AI across existing Creative Cloud subscriptions at marginal cost.
